subject: Octave AI — renewal: capacity cadence & performance recap
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@octave.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal prep — usage + capacity signal (Q1–Q2)

Hi Rafael,

Hope you’re well — we’re starting the internal renewal conversation for Octave AI and wanted to share a quick usage snapshot and ask for a short performance/ROI recap ahead of our exec review. Attached is a CSV with token spend broken down by workspace and feature (Octave-usage-Q1-Q2.csv).

Key signals from our side:
- Net token spend up ~42% QoQ driven by new summarization feature (background batch jobs).
- Weekend latency spikes have been noticeable for cached endpoints (~1200ms at peak vs 300ms weekday median).
- We expect another ~25% organic growth next quarter if we keep current commit & caching.

Ask: can Redwood provide a one-page performance summary (latency percentiles, cache hit uplift, and an ROI estimate for moving to a higher commit tier vs burst credits)? Also need a proposal for a staged capacity cadence for the renewal (1) base commit, (2) staged uplift months 3–6, (3) overflow/burst terms.

Would appreciate a short reply with availability for a 30-min sync next week. Our procurement lead is procurement@octave.ai — copy them if you need formal PO steps.

Thanks,

Sanjay Mehta
Head of Platform
Octave AI

Attachment: Octave-usage-Q1-Q2.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@octave.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — usage + capacity signal (Q1–Q2)

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Looping in Lauren (capacity / pricing) and Sean (solutions/ops) to make sure we cover both the economic and operational sides.

Quick overview we can deliver before your exec review:
- Perf summary (p50/p90/p99 by route + weekend surge comparison) — PDF (we’ll attach).
- Cache hit uplift analysis and estimated token savings with prefix caching enabled for summarization flows.
- Three-tier commit proposal (Base / Staged uplift / Burst lane) with per-token effective rates and headroom math; plus an ROI table comparing committed uplift vs on-demand spend.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll send the perf-summary.pdf and a recommended commit cadence draft by EOD tomorrow (May 20).
2) Quick 30-min sync to review — we have openings Thu 11:00–12:30 PST and Fri 09:00–12:00 PST.
3) If you want, we can include a one-page procurement checklist (PO cadence, invoice cadence, and SOW redlines) so your procurement contact has everything they need.

We’ll attach the perf-summary.pdf and a spreadsheet with the commit tiers.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: perf-summary.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@octave.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — capacity cadence & proposed commit tiers

Hi Sanjay / Rafael — following up with the capacity cadence draft and suggested economics. See the highlights below (full details in attached Excel).

Proposal summary (monthly committed token tiers):
- Tier A (Base): 120M tokens / mo — covers current steady-state inference + 10% buffer.
- Tier B (Staged uplift): 160M tokens / mo — months 3–6 after renewal; assumes activation of new summarization flow.
- Tier C (Burst lane): 220M tokens / mo — reserved for peak/holiday windows; billed as committed during the tranche month, with rollover rules.

Operational levers and expected impact:
- Prefix/KV caching: expected 18–24% token reduction for summarization flows if implemented for background jobs (notes in sheet).
- Quantization profile: recommend int8 for the summarization model variant to reduce GPU cost for Dedicated pilots without perceptible quality drop; modeled savings included.
- Autoscale buffer: we recommend a 15% burst buffer across all routes with automatic fallback to on-demand for >Tier C.

ROI snapshot (3-yr NPV rough):
- Committing to Tier B vs staying on Tier A + on-demand: modeled ~22% lower cost/year assuming growth scenario A (25% QoQ next quarter).
- Payback time on the upgrade (delta commit) estimated at 4–6 months under current usage cadence.

Links and attachments:
- Spreadsheet: Octave-commit-model.xlsx (attached)
- Drive folder with visual perf charts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Octave-RNW
- Redwood proposal draft (internal link): https://redwood.app/proposals/OCT-2027-RNW-3

If that looks reasonable, Rafael — we can convert the spreadsheet values into a short mutual action plan (MAP) and route to procurement for signature. Sanjay — any constraints from procurement on billing cadence or PO timing?

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Octave-commit-model.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@octave.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@octave.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — capacity cadence & performance recap

Thanks all — this is exactly what we needed for the exec meeting.

We’ll take Tier B as the baseline for the renewal discussion and confirm PO timing early next week. Procurement asked to confirm: billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly), and whether the burst lane can be invoiced only when used (prefer to avoid committed billing for bursts).

Availability for the sync: Friday 05/21 16:00 PST works for Rafael and Lauren on our side — can you confirm?

Sanjay
Head of Platform, Octave AI
